rv.q: This is a witty production that finds an interesting new slant of power struggle inflected by gender.

The set design by Basia Bińkowska is elegant, too, and the performances are sharp. But this is a tricky play to pull off because of its many (too many?) fevered components. Maybe it is lesser performed for good reason, or perhaps this production, full of inspired ideas, does not anchor them down enough.
The sprawling play displays its customary capacity to snare attention; we allow the far-fetched flourishes while the drops of heartfelt speech (“Hang there, like fruit, my soul…”) work a treat.
As the revelations and explanations arrive one after the other, Tang and company make the story’s contradictions something to celebrate.

The original version’s scheming Queen is replaced by a dithering Duke whose ineptitness only strengthens Cymbeline’s temperament by comparison. Innogen flees from her mother’s court disguised as a man muttering “I see a man's life is a tedious one.” Where Tang fails is wrangling the play’s black humour.
They give depth and flavour to a mediocre script.
